title: Lists and Sets
subtitle: LPUSH, RPOP, SADD, SINTER, and queue patterns
author: KERNAL

whyItExists.problem: Job queues and membership checks are fundamental to applications. Implementing a reliable job queue or social-graph follower system with just strings or a SQL table is cumbersome and slow.
whyItExists.solution: Redis Lists provide O(1) push/pop with blocking support — perfect for producer-consumer queues. Redis Sets provide O(1) add/membership-check and set operations (union, intersection, difference) for social graphs, tags, and permissions.
whyItExists.whenToUse: List: background job queues, activity feeds, chat history (bounded). Set: unique collections, social graphs, tag systems, real-time presence.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: If you need ordered results by value (not insertion order), use Sorted Sets. If you need to query across fields, use a full database.

explainModes.beginner: A List is like a queue at a coffee shop — people join at the back and are served from the front. A Set is like a bag of unique stickers — you can't have duplicates, and you can compare two bags to find common stickers.
explainModes.simple: Lists hold ordered items with O(1) push/pop at both ends. Sets hold unique items with O(1) add/check. Use BLPOP on a list to build a worker that waits for jobs. Use SINTER on two sets to find common members.
explainModes.standard: Redis Lists are doubly-linked lists (internally a quicklist of zip lists) with O(1) operations at both ends. BLPOP blocks the connection until an element is available. Redis Sets are hash tables with O(1) SADD/SISMEMBER. SINTER, SUNION, SDIFF compute set operations in O(N).
explainModes.technical: List encoding: listpack for ≤128 elements of ≤64 bytes, then quicklist (doubly-linked list of listpack nodes). Set encoding: intset for integer-only sets up to 512 members, then hash table. LMOVE atomically pops from one list and pushes to another — a reliable queue pattern that prevents message loss.
explainModes.deepDive: The reliable queue pattern uses LMOVE source dest LEFT RIGHT to atomically move a job to a 'processing' list. If the worker crashes, the job is in the processing list and can be recovered. This is the basis for Sidekiq's retry mechanism. BRPOPLPUSH (deprecated in Redis 6.2, replaced by BLMOVE) implemented the same pattern with blocking.

content.text: Redis Lists support O(1) push and pop from both ends. This makes them ideal for FIFO queues (RPUSH + BLPOP) and stacks (LPUSH + LPOP). Blocking variants wait for data rather than polling.

content.code:
# FIFO Queue: add to right, consume from left
RPUSH jobs:email "send-welcome" "send-receipt" "send-promo"
LPOP jobs:email      # "send-welcome"

# Blocking consumer (worker waits up to 30s for a job)
BLPOP jobs:email 30
# Returns: ["jobs:email", "send-receipt"]

# Stack: add and remove from same end
LPUSH history:user1 "visited page A"
LPUSH history:user1 "clicked buy"
LPOP history:user1   # "clicked buy" (most recent first)

# View without consuming
LRANGE jobs:email 0 -1   # all items
LLEN jobs:email          # count

# Trim to last 100 items (capped log)
LTRIM activity:feed 0 99

content.text: Plain BLPOP has a risk: if the worker crashes after popping but before finishing, the job is lost. LMOVE solves this by atomically moving the job to a 'processing' list.
Sets store unique strings with O(1) add, remove, and membership check. They also support powerful set operations: union, intersection, and difference.

content.code:
# Online presence
SADD online:users "alice" "bob" "carol"
SISMEMBER online:users "alice"  # 1 (is online)
SCARD online:users              # 3 (count)
SMEMBERS online:users           # all members

# Social graph
SADD user:1:following "alice" "bob"
SADD user:2:following "bob" "carol"

# Set operations
SINTER user:1:following user:2:following  # common: ["bob"]
SUNION user:1:following user:2:following  # all: ["alice","bob","carol"]
SDIFF  user:1:following user:2:following  # only user:1 follows: ["alice"]

# Move a member between sets
SMOVE online:users away:users "alice"

# Random member (useful for sampling)
SRANDMEMBER online:users 2  # 2 random members
SPOP online:users            # remove and return one random member

a.name: List
a.useWhen: Job queues, activity feeds, chat history, stacks

b.name: Set
b.useWhen: Tags, followers, online presence, permissions, unique visitors

content.text: Use BLPOP jobs:email jobs:sms 30 with multiple keys to have one worker drain multiple queues. Redis returns the key name along with the value so you know which queue fired.

questions.question: What does BLPOP do when the list is empty?
options: Blocks the connection until an element is pushed or timeout expires
questions.explanation: BLPOP blocks the connection (not the entire server) until an element is available, up to the specified timeout. This avoids polling loops in workers.

questions.question: What command finds the members that exist in BOTH set A and set B?
questions.explanation: SINTER returns the intersection — members that exist in ALL specified sets. SUNION returns all members from all sets. SDIFF returns members in the first set not present in the others.

questions.question: Why is LMOVE better than BLPOP for a reliable job queue?
options: LMOVE atomically moves the job to a 'processing' list, so a crashed worker doesn't lose the job
LMOVE works with Cluster; BLPOP does not
LMOVE supports blocking; BLPOP does not
questions.explanation: With plain BLPOP, if a worker crashes after popping a job but before finishing it, the job is lost. LMOVE moves it to a 'processing' list atomically — the job can be recovered from there if the worker fails.

faq.q: How do I implement a task queue with Redis?
faq.a: RPUSH to enqueue jobs, BLPOP to consume them. For reliability, use LMOVE to atomically move jobs to a 'processing' list before working on them, so crashes don't lose jobs.

faq.q: What is the maximum number of members in a Redis Set?
faq.a: Up to 2^32 - 1 (over 4 billion) members. In practice, large sets use significant memory — monitor SCARD and size accordingly.

faq.q: Can I expire individual set members?
faq.a: No. TTL applies to the whole key. If you need per-member expiry, use a Sorted Set with timestamps as scores and periodically ZREMRANGEBYSCORE to remove old members.

examples: Sidekiq (Ruby) uses Redis Lists as the core of its background job queue
Social apps store follower/following sets in Redis for O(1) mutual friend lookups
